official_measurement_examples.name: BMV grades
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England guidance defines best and most versatile agricultural land as ALC Grades 1, 2 and 3a.

official_measurement_examples.name: 20 hectare consultation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England guidance says LPAs must consult Natural England for non-agricultural proposals likely to cause loss of 20 hectares or more of BMV land when the proposal is not in accordance with an approved development plan.

official_measurement_examples.name: Strategic map limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states 1:250,000 ALC overview maps are not sufficiently detailed or accurate for assessment of individual fields or sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: Predictive ALC 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra's Predictive ALC dataset updated 1 July 2026 provides a national strategic view and subdivides Grade 3 according to current ALC guidance, but remains a strategic-scale product.

official_measurement_examples.name: Post-1988 survey polygons
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's post-1988 polygon dataset updated 19 June 2026 records survey grade and job number and uses climate, site and soil criteria; it represents surveyed areas rather than universal field-level coverage.

official_measurement_examples.name: Provisional map limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The provisional ALC dataset is derived from older 1:250,000 mapping and does not subdivide Grade 3 into 3a and 3b for site-specific BMV decisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Detailed survey precedence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England advises using post-1988 detailed site surveys where available and carrying out a new detailed survey where suitable site data do not exist.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: ALC or BMV status is an input to planning assessment and consultation; it is not planning permission, refusal, ownership evidence or proof of development capacity.

core_rules: ALC grade is planning evidence not a complete planning decision
BMV means Grades 1 2 and 3a and must not include 3b by assumption
a strategic 1:250000 ALC map is not a field-scale survey
predictive ALC output is not a substitute for detailed site survey where precision is required
provisional Grade 3 mapping does not distinguish 3a from 3b
post-1988 survey coverage must not be extrapolated beyond surveyed geometry
Natural England consultation trigger is not automatic refusal
planning permission is not evidence that agricultural land quality is low
ALC does not determine land ownership or access rights
soil handling and restoration requirements are distinct from ALC classification
historic survey data must retain survey date scale and methodology
new detailed surveys may supersede strategic mapping for site assessment
Planning Data ingestion status must not silently upgrade source precision
BMV policy protection does not reserve or remove infrastructure capacity
no parcel agricultural-land clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
